skills_considered.reason: The complete fingerprinted HTML was supplied; only figures and supplement status required retrieval.
The study qualifies gene-environment susceptibility but provides no disease-relevant therapeutic hypothesis.
NMBA is an experimental carcinogen, not a proposed intervention.
Canonical promotion remains reserved for the operator's BATCH_COMMIT.

group_assessment.weighting: PubMed ESearch on 2026-08-11 returned 137 Aqeilan RI author records and 64 WWOX title/abstract records. This is a primary WWOX experimental oncology lab. The large carcinogen-response contrast is first-hand; strict haploinsufficiency is an interpretation because the remaining allele was not genotyped in tumors.

queries.query: WWOX AND (forestomach OR esophageal) AND carcinogenesis

field_density.note: The exact forestomach/esophageal carcinogenesis intersection is sparse. The broader heterozygous literature is larger but heterogeneous and cannot substitute for this challenged adult design.

multihop.note: All 18 references were enumerated. Seventeen resolve to PMIDs; the American Cancer Society facts-and-figures report has no PMID. Reference 7, the foundational knockout paper, is read in this same batch. The FHIT analogy is not used as WWOX evidence.

corpus_crossquery.query: Where does PMID 17575124 occur and which carrier/context claims does its challenged heterozygote design qualify?
corpus_crossquery.note: Thirteen disease-model files contain the PMID, including CORPUS P282. The paper qualifies CLAIM 032: normal unchallenged heterozygote physiology and strong carcinogen susceptibility can both be true because they measure different contexts.

retraction_check.result: Repository retraction preflight on 2026-08-11 returned no retraction or expression-of-concern flag for PMID 17575124.

verbatim_locators.source_fulltext_indexed_evidence: Local PMC HTML identifies PMID 17575124, PMCID PMC2621009 and DOI 10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-07-1081 and contains the complete body, Table 1, two captions and 18 references. The repository supplement endpoint reported non-open-access and the article names no supplement.

entries.proposition: NMBA challenge produced a large genotype difference in tumor incidence and multiplicity.
entries.snippet: 96% (25 out of 26) of Wwox+/- mice developed forestomach tumors compared with 29% (10 out of 34) of wild-type controls

entries.proposition: Invasive carcinoma occurred only in the heterozygous group in this experiment.
entries.snippet: 27% (7 of 26) of Wwox+/- mice had invasive SCC in the forestomach (Fig. 1B, d and g), as compared with none of the Wwox+/+ mice

entries.proposition: The experiment measured residual protein staining, not the genetic state of the second allele.
entries.snippet: Wwox staining in the same forestomach section was weak and diffuse in epithelial cells showing dysplasia (Fig. 1C, c), and very weak in the invasive tumor areas

entries.proposition: The challenge design administered NMBA to both genotype groups and had no untreated arm.
entries.snippet: Thirty-four Wwox+/+ mice and 26 Wwox+/- mice (10-12 weeks old) were given six intragastric doses of NMBA
entries.anchor: Materials and Methods, NMBA-induced forestomach carcinogenesis study

entries.proposition: Table 1 preserves the exact SCC and tumor denominators underlying the susceptibility conclusion.
Figure 1 supplies gross, histological and staining evidence across all seventeen subpanels.
entries.snippet: The image shows gross WT and heterozygous forestomachs, H&E/PCNA/KRT14 series and progressive loss of Wwox staining from epithelium to SCC.
